President Trump vowed to retaliate against what he described as unfair fines imposed by the European Union on Apple and other U.S. tech giants. Details below.

"America is not Europe's 'ATM'"

According to CNBC, President Trump posted a lengthy message on Truth Social, threatening to impose "massive" tariffs on the EU in response to fines the bloc has levied on Apple and other U.S. tech giants.

In the post, Trump referenced the EU's recent €890 million fine against Google over allegations it favored its own services in violation of the Digital Markets Act. He also listed previous fines against Apple, Meta, and Amazon, accusing the EU of penalizing American companies "without justification."

He further threatened that the EU would pay a "very heavy price" for what he called "illegal and immoral behavior," and pledged that those "penalties will be completely overturned."

Top Comments on CCATX

Oh my god, I'm so tired of being humiliated by this childish, ignorant, infantile man. I have never voted for him, and he should never have been allowed to hold public office after his first term. Do I agree with everything in the Digital Markets Act? No—I actually think some of it is absurd—but this is not a political issue, nor is it specifically targeted at companies from any one country.

This isn't the first time Trump has threatened tariffs in response to foreign penalties against Apple and other U.S. tech firms. His administration earlier characterized the EU's 2025 fines against Apple and Meta as "economic extortion," while warning that any country penalizing American businesses would face trade retaliation.

Regarding Apple specifically, the $15 billion fine Trump referenced appears to relate to the EU's long-running tax dispute with the company. In 2024, Europe's top court ruled that Ireland must recover €13 billion in unpaid taxes from Apple—not that the EU itself collected the fine. Apple was also fined €570 million in April 2025 for violating the Digital Markets Act.
